_authority: EVERY ROW BELOW WAS DERIVED, NOT REMEMBERED, and the derivation is the interesting part. The audit asked the one question no gate in this repo was asking of this lane: of the grammar's 126 declared named node types (124 from node-types.json plus the universal ERROR/MISSING pair), which ones does the analyzer NEVER NAME? The set came from the analyzer's own source — its switch-case labels, read by script/m60/solidity-completeness-spec.ts — not from an inventory kept by hand. The 23 the current analyzer does not name are a WRAPPER/PASSTHROUGH population rather than a gap population: each one's content is read by its children, is a literal/keyword, or is an operator spelling rather than an entity. 126 is the universe the completion gate asks about, not the 124 a reader sees in node-types.json — that difference is ERROR and MISSING, which every parser produces and neither inventory lists. That is a strong claim and it is checked from both ends rather than asserted: the generator REFUSES to write a section whose buckets do not cover the universe exactly once, and --verify-silence re-parses live sources to confirm each silent type really is silent and each wrapper's child really does the work. Three handoff claims for this lane were refuted by measurement and are recorded where they bite: the '27 never-exercised types' figure is a property of a 60-file DRAW (it is 12 over the full 389-file production corpus); 'the corpus under-represents Yul' is FALSE, so Yul is analysed as a first-class sub-language rather than ruled out; and '0 damage' was measured on the draw and also holds at full size. Evidence: validation/m60/results/solidity-type-census.json.
_wave: M60 Solidity lane. The grammar is pinned byte-identical to the npm tarball tree-sitter-solidity@1.2.13 with ZERO local patches (script/m14/verify-grammar-pins.ts, LANES.solidity), which is the only provenance kind structurally immune to the failure the PowerShell lane hit — a record claiming 8 patches against bytes containing 7. There is no build step and none is wanted: the package publishes a prebuilt wasm, so the bytes are the maintainer's own artifact, and a local rebuild's sha is not a function of its source across toolchain versions.

handled_verified._description: The analyzer has a case for the node type AND the case emits something — a symbol, an edge, or a payload field the store reads. 'Verified' means a fixture or the full-corpus census demonstrates it: the fixture set is validation/m14/fixtures/solidity/ (34 fixtures, all passing — the runner's own count, script/m14/run-fixtures.ts --lang solidity) and every corpus frequency in the corpusCounts map is measured over all 389 production files of solidity@32b5b8c4, draw digest c1531019, through the production parseFile.

internal_silent._description: The analyzer has NO case for the node type and correctly emits nothing: a literal, a keyword, a transparent wrapper whose content is read by its children, or a payload field collected into a declared symbol field rather than published. Every entry names WHICH child or WHICH payload does the work — 'it is a wrapper' is not a reason until you say which wrapper. Nothing in this bucket is a silence left to look like an oversight.

gap._description: Confirmed missing emission, numbered G1.. and tracked as work. EMPTY, and the emptiness is a measurement rather than an omission: every one of the 124 declared named types is classified, the 25 the analyzer does not name are each verified silent against live code, and there is no node type whose content reaches nothing.

design_decision._description: An owner ruling where silence or an unusual shape is a DECISION rather than a consequence of the grammar. Each entry states the decision and why, and each is load-bearing for the lane's shape: the public-getter publication, the compilation-unit export surface, the extends-vs-implements split, and the four node types whose silence is argued rather than derived.

decisions.decision: internal_silent — and the refusal is by SOURCE LINE, not by subtree
decisions.rationale: SOL-6. An `ERROR` subtree is text the parser could not parse, so every symbol and relationship under it is a guess. The subtree is not the whole region: on validation/m14/fixtures/solidity/recovery-regions-sol6.sol the parser emits an ERROR covering only `is not ) valid solidity ( at` plus a MISSING `;`, and the tokens `this` and `all` are SIBLINGS of that ERROR node, outside its subtree. The first version of SOL-6 skipped the subtree and published a symbol named `all` and a type reference `this` — the parser's guess about garbage, stored as graph fact. So the rule is a pre-pass over ERROR/MISSING line spans, consulted by both emit helpers. The corpus cannot exercise it: 0 damaged files over all 389 production files, which is exactly why the fixture forces an ERROR on purpose.

decisions.decision: internal_silent — the more dangerous of the pair, for a stated reason
decisions.rationale: A MISSING node is a token the parser INSERTED so it could keep going, so it carries no error of its own: `tree.rootNode.hasError` is true because of it, but the node is fabricated content rather than a report of damage. Every instrument in this repo keyed on `hasError` therefore sees the FILE and not the insertion. SOL-6's line-range rule covers it: the inserted token's line is in the recovery set, so nothing is emitted from it. Pinned by recovery-regions-sol6, whose parser emits a MISSING `;` on line 7.

decisions.decision: internal_silent — the named fields bind PARAMETERS, which are not symbols
decisions.rationale: SOL-10. `f({x: 1, y: 2})` is the modern named-argument form; each `call_struct_argument` names a parameter of `f`. Parameters are collected into the function's `parameters` payload and are deliberately not published as symbols, so an edge naming one would point at nothing the store holds. 33 occurrences.

decisions.decision: internal_silent — same reasoning as call_struct_argument, and the two spellings are kept distinct
decisions.rationale: SOL-10. `S { a: 1 }` is the pre-0.8.8 spelling and its `struct_field_assignment` names a FIELD of `S`. The field IS published — as a member of `S`, owned by `S` — so an edge from the USE SITE would resolve to a member of a DIFFERENT owner, which is a different lie from the one SOL-1 is about. The `type:` field carries the struct name and does produce the call. 13 occurrences, disjoint from the 33 above.

decisions.decision: internal_silent — it names an OPERATOR, not an entity
decisions.rationale: `using {Op.plus as +} for Price global` (grammar.js:53). The aliased OPERATOR `+` is not a name and cannot be a symbol; the aliased FUNCTION `Op.plus` is a `using_alias` child and IS handled, emitting `references -> Op`. 4 occurrences.

decisions.decision: internal_silent — both of its children are handled, so it adds nothing
decisions.rationale: grammar.js:53 — a `using_directive` holds EITHER a `type_alias` (`using L for T`) or a `using_alias` (`using {f, g} for T global`), and both have their own case emitting a `references` edge to the named entity, plus a `uses` type reference for the `source:` type. 102 occurrences, and verified on both forms.

decisions.decision: internal_silent — no edge, and the skip is provably lossless
decisions.rationale: SOL-8. An EVM opcode is not a callable function: `yul_function_call`'s `function:` field is `choice(yul_identifier, yul_evm_builtin)`, so `add(1,2)` in assembly is an opcode. Emitting `calls -> add` would put 2,800 rows naming a name no Solidity identifier can hold. LOSSLESS because the lexer always spells a bare `add` in Yul as the builtin, so a user-defined Yul function can never be named `add` — there is no name this silence could swallow.

excluded.label: part_of
excluded.from: grammar-remedy-ruled — R1: the pinned grammar is npm 1.2.13, the latest published build, and its 124 named types contain no part/template/include node. R2: a clone+patch could name a new node, but Solidity has no part-file directive to expose: `import` names a MODULE and creates binding scope, while `part_of` is a compilation unit that SHARES another library's single scope and imports nothing. A patched node would have to invent the semantics, which a grammar cannot do. R3: `import_directive` is already `imports` (932 edges), declaration nesting is `contains`, and no existing node type carries a part relation. THE CORPUS AGBREES: 0 part-file directives over the 421-file admitted population. AND THE SEMANTIC HALF IS THE ONE THAT DECIDES IT. The vocabulary's `part_of` is a PART-FILE directive — a compilation unit that SHARES another library's single scope rather than importing it (dart `part 'x.dart'` / `part of 'x.dart'`, src/ast/types.ts PartOf). Solidity has no such directive: a file's dependency on another file is an `import`, which names a MODULE and creates binding scope, and this lane already publishes it per path as `imports` (932 edges). The two constructs a reader might mistake for it are both otherwise recorded: 0 nodes naming part/template/component constructs among the served grammar's 124 named types (validation/m14/measurements/solidity-grammar-nodes.json), and declaration nesting — a struct or enum declared inside a contract — is CONTAINMENT, already emitted as `contains` (6,531 edges indexed). excluded.label: mixes_in
excluded.from: ontological — THE LADDER WAS WALKED AND R3 WAS TRIED, WHICH IS THE STRONGEST FORM OF THIS RULING. R1: the latest published build (1.2.13) exposes `using_directive`, which the analyzer already parses; no published build adds a member-set composition node because the language has none. R2: a grammar patch can expose syntax but cannot make `using L for T` add a member to T — the directive binds member LOOKUP within a scope, it does not extend the type. R3: the emission was implemented and published (27 rows) and WITHDRAWN the same day after the vocabulary's own contract failed on it. AN EMISSION WAS TRIED, PUBLISHED, AND WITHDRAWN THE SAME DAY (SOL-24, 2026-10-27), so the construct was measured and the value was made to carry it before the vocabulary's own contract failed on it. `mixes_in` is (src/ast/types.ts) "a class COMPOSES a mixin into its SUPERTYPE CHAIN … the mixin is a supertype MEMBER", and every other user of the value satisfies that: PHP trait `use` flattens the trait's members into the class's method table and subclasses inherit them (real-php-analyzer.ts isTraitUse); Go embedding PROMOTES the embedded type's methods and fields into the outer struct's method set (real-go-analyzer.ts); ruby `include` and zig `usingnamespace` likewise put the members where the composing unit can be asked for them. SOLIDITY ADDS NO MEMBER: after `using MathLib for Price`, `Price` is still `uint128`, has no member `double`, and its ABI and inheritance chain are untouched — `p.double()` binds as `MathLib.double(p)` only where a directive is in scope, and `global` widens the SCOPE, not the type. THE COMPOSING ACTOR IS THEREFORE THE SCOPE, NOT THE TYPE, so the withdrawn row had the wrong source as well as the wrong relation. THE COST WAS CONCRETE: src/intelligence/graph/graph-engine.ts ranks `mixes_in` as supertype composition between `implements` and `renders`, and src/intelligence/analysis/complexity.ts carries it in the coupling set, so `Price -> MathLib` read as a supertype Price does not have. THE CONSTRUCT IS COUNTED, NOT DISMISSED, over the whole 421-file admitted population (validation/m14/measurements/solidity-extended-census.json and script/m14/tmp/sol24-mixes-counters.mts): 124 `using_directive` sites in 76 files = 27 with a declared host and a single library (23 struct, 3 interface, 1 struct+type) + 54 `for *` (no host) + 39 primitive hosts + 4 braced function sets, and ZERO of the 27 adds a member to the host. THE DEPENDENCY SURVIVES THE REFUSAL: the `type_alias` case already publishes `references` to the library for every one of these directives (all 27 resolve), and the control fixture asserts that row beside the prohibition. THE NEAREST VALUE IS NOT A FALLBACK EITHER: `uses` would be false in the same way (the directive does more than read the name) and would double a name-read row `references` already carries.
